Governance and oversight: Governance for the Product is exercised through a formal senior‑management and Board reporting structure: ultimate oversight rests with the Board via the Board Risk Committee (which receives quarterly financial‑crime MI and Product updates as set out in the Board Risk Committee pack), and day‑to‑day responsibility is held by the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) and the MLRO supported by a Product governance forum (Global Payments Oversight Committee/Product Governance Committee) that brings together Group Compliance, Legal, Operations, Risk, Finance and regional compliance leads and meets on a monthly cadence; local compliance heads in each operating jurisdiction have direct reporting lines into Group Compliance and are required to escalate material AML/CTF/sanctions matters to the CCO/MLRO and, where appropriate, to the Board Risk Committee and Internal Audit; MI on onboarding/KYC coverage, alert volumes and disposition, sanctions hits, SAR filing metrics and remediation progress is produced weekly for operational owners, monthly for senior management and quarterly for the Board Risk Committee; Internal Audit provides independent testing on an annual cycle and conducts targeted deep‑dives of remediation workstreams, and the governance framework and delegated authorities are documented in the Group AML/CTF Policy and Product‑specific procedures (see appended policy extracts and Board pack).

We have imposed enhanced governance for these workstreams (weekly remediation steering meetings chaired by the CCO, monthly reporting to the Board Risk Committee, and direct involvement of regional heads) and will align Product go‑live to the completion and independent validation of the defined critical milestones that materially affect high‑risk cross‑border monitoring; lower‑priority data‑quality items may proceed on a controlled post‑launch remediation timetable under documented compensating controls, but we will confirm a final launch decision once validation evidence for the critical milestones is available.

To: [Name], Case Officer
Subject: Clarifications re: Independent validation, Hub‑3 reliance and conditional launch — Digital Payments Product

Thank you for your note and the opportunity to clarify our approach; please find responses below and the referenced validation test plan outline and corridor mapping spreadsheet attached.

1. Independent validation — scope and methodology  
As described in our submission, independent validation will be performed by Internal Audit and/or the Model/Controls testing function (Financial Crime Effectiveness) after the relevant remediation workstreams for FC‑02 and FC‑01 are complete. The intended scope and methodology (summarised from the validation test plan outline) are: data‑integrity verification (data‑lineage/ETL checks, attribute completeness and reconciliation between source feeds and the monitoring dataset); rule‑execution testing (unit and integration tests to confirm rules run as designed across the production rule engine); back‑testing and rule‑performance assessment (replay/back‑test over a representative historical period to confirm alert generation and to identify missed alerts); sample‑based case review (stratified sampling across high‑risk corridors, random samples and edge cases for investigator review); and quantitative metrics (coverage of monitored flows, alert rates, disposition rates, false‑positive indicators and indicators of potential false negatives). Findings will be triaged by severity; material or critical validation findings will be escalated to the remediation steering group and GFCC immediately and reported to the BRC, with agreed remediation actions and timelines recorded in the remediation tracker; less severe findings will be tracked via the remediation process and reported in monthly PGC‑DP/GFCC updates.

2. Operational definition and classification of Hub‑3‑reliant flows  
Operationally, a flow, corridor or client segment is classified as “materially reliant on Regional Hub 3’s monitoring infrastructure” where any of the following apply (each of which is explicitly applied in the corridor mapping spreadsheet): (a) the monitoring of the corridor/flow is routed to Hub 3 with no equivalent parallel monitoring route; (b) detection depends on Hub‑3‑specific transaction/customer attributes that are not available to other hubs; or (c) a material proportion of alerting for that corridor (as identified in historical MI) is generated by rules executed only in Hub 3. The corridor mapping attached to this response identifies which proposed Product flows meet these criteria (the mapping includes the per‑corridor routing, the monitoring owner, and an explicit “Hub‑3‑reliant” flag); at a high level, the mapping distinguishes cross‑border corridors routed to Hub 3 (classified as Hub‑3‑reliant) from flows monitored by local/regional hubs or by platform‑level screening that are not Hub‑3‑reliant. We have attached the corridor mapping spreadsheet for your review and can provide a short extract listing the Hub‑3‑reliant corridors if helpful.

3. Conditional launch — circumstances, compensating controls and governance  
Consistent with your closing letter, our default position is that flows materially reliant on Hub 3 will not be placed into production until FC‑02 and FC‑01 are complete and have passed independent validation. In the event we were to propose a conditional launch plan, it would only be considered where: (i) documented compensating controls are in place and demonstrably effective (examples would include heightened manual review of Hub‑3‑routed transactions, temporary transaction thresholds, mandatory escalation for specific corridors and enhanced case‑management workflows); (ii) the compensating controls and the conditional launch plan (including clearly defined, evidentiary milestones and acceptance criteria) are shared with the Authority in advance; and (iii) targeted independent validation has confirmed the critical monitoring elements underpinning the conditional plan. Governance for any conditional plan would include continued oversight by the remediation steering group with weekly reporting, monthly review at PGC‑DP and GFCC and quarterly visibility to the BRC, and rapid escalation to those fora for material issues. At this stage we are not submitting a conditional launch plan; we remain open to discussing such an approach with the Authority if the Authority wishes to consider it and if the evidentiary and governance conditions above are met.

Attachments: validation_test_plan_outline.pdf; corridor_mapping.xlsx; remediation_tracker_extract.pdf

We would be happy to provide the specific list of Hub‑3‑reliant corridors from the corridor mapping and to discuss any element of the validation approach at your convenience.

Kind regards,
[General Counsel]

3) Internal talking points for a potential follow‑up call (6–8 bullets)

If you want, I will prepare: (a) the corridor extract listing Hub‑3‑reliant corridors for Authority review; and (b) a short validation‑methodology annex with sample frame sizes and back‑test horizon for immediate circulation to Internal Audit/Model Risk for sign‑off.
